corrected_claim: Culp's Hill, 2 Jul: Geary's division formed on the ridge about 05:00 and Greene's brigade about 06:00; breastworks of logs, cord-wood, stones and earth went up at once and gave good cover within "a few hours" (finish digit unreadable in the OCR, 10:00 or 12:00). A pre-existing stone wall stood behind the line: 30-75 yd behind the First Division works (four witnesses), 200-300 yd behind Kane's and Ruger's works (two witnesses): carried as scenarios (sector defaults under DD-F2-06, no single point).

subclaims.claim: Greene's brigade took position on the crest of Culp's Hill on the morning of 2 Jul (about 06:00 by Greene's OCR "G a. m."; the division at 05:00 by Geary; at sunrise by Greene 1893) and began to intrench at once.
subclaims.why: Hour: 05:00 (Geary) to 06:00 (Greene); the digit in Greene's report is OCR-read.

subclaims.claim: Greene's brigade (Greene's order) built breastworks "of the covering height" of logs, cord-wood, stones and earth; Geary's whole line did the same "immediately".
The main line was a good breastwork "in a few hours", "completed early in the day, almost exclusively by the Third Brigade"; Greene's report fixes the finish at "1? o'clock" (OCR "13").
subclaims.why: Window end 09:00-10:00 (PDF default) or about 12:00 is not decidable from the OCR digit; both fit "a few hours" from 06:00.

subclaims.claim: A pre-existing stone wall lay behind the breastworks; witnesses place it 30-75 yd behind the First Division works (Williams < 50 yd; Ruger about 75 yd; McDougall about 40 paces; Price 125 ft) and 200-300 yd behind Kane's and Ruger's intrenchments (Geary, Greene).
subclaims.why: Four First Division witnesses agree within 30-75 yd for a wall behind McDougall's brigade; two Second Division witnesses give 200-300 yd for a wall held by the enemy on the night of 2 Jul. Whether these are one or two walls is not stated by any source: the distances are carried as scenarios (no default).

subclaims.claim: The 145th NY repaired the stone wall during 2 Jul until 18:30.

The 3rd Wisconsin built breastworks of earth and rails and threw down stone walls and fences in its front on the east bank of Rock Creek on 2 Jul before 18:00; the 27th Indiana line used rails, timber and stone.
The enemy held the original intrenched line and the stone wall on the night of 2 Jul.
The line was about 300 yd long on the morning of 2 Jul.
subclaims.why: Only source GD-219 (a blog); no OR or regimental text gives a length.

subclaims.claim: The work may have finished about noon (Gettysburg Daily).
subclaims.why: Blog source; the OR digit is unreadable.

subclaims.claim: The First Division (Ruger/Williams) built log breastworks along the entire crest "at once" on 2 Jul, breastworks of logs, rocks and earth along the whole line (Ruger).
Geary's division (Greene, Kane, Candy in support) threw up breastworks along its whole line "immediately" on the morning of 2 Jul.
Kane's brigade, ordered into line "soon after" he assumed command at 06:00 on 2 Jul, threw up its breastwork "before sundown"; Kane gives no morning hour.
subclaims.why: Kane's own report; it bounds the Kane-sector work between 06:00 and sundown and does not support the printed "Jul 2 morning" for that sector (the same conflict is carried at fence-1 E-07).

subclaims.claim: Wadsworth's First Corps men built breastworks on Culp's Hill on 2 Jul morning.

subclaims.claim: The 147th PA (Candy) occupied a stone fence in front of the enemy after several rounds from a battery that opened at 03:45 on 3 Jul, and at 05:00 was ordered to charge and carry the stone wall held by the enemy, which the enemy then abandoned.
subclaims.why: Candy gives the occupation after 03:45 (not at 03:45); Geary gives the order at 05:00. That the "stone fence" of Candy and the "stone wall" of Geary are one wall is not stated.

corrected_claim: Peach Orchard/Sherfy fences, 2 Jul: a rail fence stood west of the Emmitsburg road on the night of 1-2 Jul; Union troops pulled down fences and walls from after midnight to about 11:00 (26th PA, 86th NY, Humphreys' front; cleared by about 09:00 at the orchard); other fences stood in the afternoon (3rd Maine to 16:00, 110th PA before 15:30, Sherfy stable and garden fence after 16:30, road fence at the Sherfy house in the evening); rails lay in the orchard at 01:00 on 3 Jul. The printed "destroyed afternoon-evening 2 Jul" has no source.

subclaims.claim: A rail fence ran 30-40 rods west of the Emmitsburg road and was the 4th Maine's picket line on the night of 1-2 Jul; Union pickets held the Sherfy western fence and hedgerow.

Union troops pulled down fences on the morning of 2 Jul: the 26th PA (after midnight; detailed in the morning "in front of the division"), the 86th NY (35 men under Capt. Baker, 10:00-11:00, "all stone walls and fences in our front to the Emmitsburg road"), the Peach Orchard fences already cleared at about 09:00 (New York battery), fences removed in Humphreys' front (hour not stated), and, in a partisan retrospective, "all the fences and stone walls" by Sickles.
subclaims.why: Two independent OR reports (Bodine, Higgins) plus the 26th PA regimental narrative (same regiment as Bodine) and a battery witness. The Humphreys passage has no hour; R006 is partisan. NPS (2024): "Although Union forces removed many of the north-south fences prior to the second day's battle".

subclaims.claim: Some fences still stood around the Peach Orchard and Sherfy buildings during the afternoon of 2 Jul: the fence bounding the orchard on the south-west side (3rd Maine, until about 16:00), the peach orchard fence (110th PA, before 15:30), Sherfy's stable and garden fence (Thompson's battery, after 16:30), the Emmitsburg Road fence at the Sherfy house (114th PA, evening).
Fence rails lay in the Peach Orchard at about 01:00 on 3 Jul (Alexander made a bed of them).
The Sherfy orchard and fences were "destroyed" on the afternoon-evening of 2 Jul.
subclaims.why: No primary describes a destruction event, its time or which segments; PDF key SS-Sherfy is a lead only.

subclaims.claim: The peach trees of the Sherfy orchard were destroyed.
